findings.location: retail[0] What Is Driving It / Smart Money View (Peloton lead)
findings.issue: Chronology: the promoted Peloton lead re-cited the takeover headlines the 2022-02-08 Peloton item had just used (CNBC 'why a deal might not happen' twice, Wedbush's Apple case), so the same caution appeared twice in the lead and the smart-money split partly recycled yesterday's item.
findings.resolution: Removed the recycled CNBC and Wedbush citations; What Is Driving It now states the stacked turnaround-plus-bid premium as interpretation, and Smart Money View rests on 8 February evidence (Blackwells n0758, investor slides n0838, Yahoo Finance's board critique n0832). Only the BBC exploring-a-takeover report (n0651) remains as background.

findings.issue: 'The market treated it as relief, not loss' overstated the reaction: NVDA rose 1.54% while SOXX rose 2.53%, so Nvidia lagged its own sector on the termination day.
findings.resolution: Reworded to 'the market shrugged off the loss' and added the SOXX +2.53% comparison from the card; intro changed from 'cheer' to 'shrug off a dead deal'.

findings.issue: Chronology: fourth straight edition with a crypto item; the break reused the 20-day-level-close test that the 2022-02-08 lead had just used, a repeated caution.
findings.resolution: Kept secondary on newly published 8 February evidence only; replaced the level test with the seizure-day price reaction (BTC +0.63%, DOGE -4.33%) and added The Art Newspaper's report of the US Treasury NFT money-laundering study (n0953).

findings.issue: Chronology: the daily-reset decay lesson repeated the 2022-02-04 TQQQ item's break almost verbatim.
findings.resolution: Cut to the card comparison (SOXL -22.33% vs SOXX -6.30% over 20 sessions) and the point that one relief day has not repaired January.

findings.issue: 'redemption story in three sessions': the rally ran over the 7 and 8 February sessions (the 4 February session rose only 1.44% before the WSJ report).
Intro said all three trades ride the kitchen-sink mechanism; AMC's lease news and the Arm termination are not kitchen-sink resets.
findings.resolution: Intro now names Peloton as the clearest case of the mechanism.

findings.issue: The MarketWatch meme-era tax-bill headline was also the 2022-02-08 lead's historical analog; here it serves a different role (winners' selling as supply).
findings.resolution: Retained; different role, within window (stamped 2022-02-07), and the AMC catalyst itself (n0754, n0753) is new.

findings.issue: All cited IDs resolved in the 2022-02-09 feed (stamps 2022-02-07 to 2022-02-08; company news within seven days); card numbers checked (PTON, NDX, 2Y, SPOT, AMC, GME, BTC, DOGE, NVDA, SOXX, MRVL, SOXL). Peloton CEO change, Nvidia–Arm termination and Bitfinex-linked seizure/arrests used as known; no Disney/Uber/Toyota results. scope_limits: Headlines only (no article bodies); the card is the sole price source; the 2022-02-01 to 02-08 retail drafts and notes were read as editorial memory only. No later-date files were read.
